summary: Baileys fork covertly auto-follows author's WhatsApp newsletter channel and aliases crypto dependency to a mutable author-controlled tag
details: dzyhaxz-baileys is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library that, on every WhatsApp `connection.open` event, silently calls `sock.newsletterFollow` for a hardcoded channel ID `120363411407993897@newsletter` with `autoFollowChannels` defaulting to true. The README explicitly states 'No hidden auto-follow: Channel operations (sock.newsletterFollow) are strictly explicit', directly contradicting the shipped behavior — any application built on this library causes its WhatsApp-authenticated users to follow the author's channel without consent. Separately, `package.json` aliases the Signal protocol crypto library to an author-owned package via a mutable dist-tag: `"libsignal": "npm:dzyhaxz-libsignal@latest"`, with no version pin. The aliased module provides the ECDH curve primitives used by `lib/Utils/crypto.js` for WhatsApp end-to-end key agreement, and `md5`/`hkdf` are additionally re-exported from the author-controlled `@rexxhayanasi/wangcap-id-bridge`. Each install resolves whatever bytes the publisher currently points `latest` at. The auto-follow uses the installer's WhatsApp identity for reach-padding (no credential theft, no RCE, no account takeover), and the aliased crypto dependency has not been observed to contain malicious bytes in this version — but the combination is a deceptive cover-story and a weaponizable supply-chain shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
